target: A: Porosity & Water Saturation (Interactive Petrophysics 2018 help decompile)
source_pages_read: basicloganalysis.htm (in-scope adjacent: only page stating a/m/n/Rw defaults)
extraction_rules: Every numeric value is quoted from the manual verbatim. No rounding, unit conversion, or knowledge-supplied values.
swequationsandmethodology.htm contains 121 rasterized equation images (embimNN.gif). Those formulas are NOT recoverable and are NOT reconstructed.
Many equations rasterized on the methodology page appear in plain ASCII on swparameters.htm; those are marked recoverable_ascii and recorded as evidence of which variant IP uses.
Tier B entries record method name + the citation the manual gives; SandiBumi reimplements from the primary paper.

methods.name: Density porosity

parameters.name: Rho GD
parameters.default: If a Rho GD is not entered then it is assumed to be 2.71.
parameters.note: Matrix grain density; used when GD source = param. Default statement appears in the 2-mineral lithology / Neutron branch.

parameters.name: GD source
parameters.note: Options: Fixed value entered as a parameter; Variable value entered as a curve; Multi-mineral (grain density from mineral volumes using TRUE mineral densities). Multi-mineral 'is the default setting if the multi-mineral options are activated'.

parameters.name: Rho Wet Clay
parameters.note: 'A value must be entered if a density tool is selected on the set-up window.'

parameters.name: Rho Dry Clay
parameters.note: Used for calculating clay total porosity, PhiT Clay.

parameters.name: PhiT Clay
parameters.note: 'If a cell is left blank, PhiT Clay will be calculated from the Rho Dry Clay and Rho Wet Clay parameter entries.'

parameters.name: Rho Sxo zone
parameters.note: 'If Rho Sxo zone is blank the value is calculated from the Rmf parameter. In oil-based mud Rho Sxo is calculated from Rw if the cell/column is left blank.'

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable (embim44). Named terms: matrix density (embim45), input bulk density log (embim46), wet clay density (embim47), filtrate density (embim48), apparent hydrocarbon density (embim49), Vcl, Sxo.
caveats: 2-mineral lithology from the Density method: 'A fixed lithology for an input Rho GD is assumed. 2.65 100% sand, 2.71 100% lime, 2.85 100% Dolomite. Input Rho GD between these end points will result in a linear extrapolation between the end points. For example an input Rho GD of 2.68 will result in 50% Sandstone and 50% Limestone.'

methods.name: Neutron porosity

parameters.name: Neu matrix

parameters.name: Neu Form Sal

'If the Neutron hydrocarbon apparent hydrogen index (NeuHyHI) is entered as a parameter then the Neutron excavation factor (Exfact) will be set at 0.0.'
To use the raw neutron with no matrix or hydrocarbon correction, verbatim parameter set: 'Neu Matrix = 0.0 / Matrix Density = Blank / NeuHyHI = 1.0'

methods.name: Neutron/Density porosity (with 4 variable-solver flags)

parameters.name: Variable Sxo
parameters.note: 'Set to On to calculate Sxo from the Neutron Density separation. This overrides the normal Sxo calculation from the input Rxo curve or the Invasion factor. The result is limited to be greater than Sw (WBM) or less than Sw (OBM). It is also limited to be less than the Sxo limit (WBM).'

parameters.name: Variable Hc Den
parameters.note: 'Set to On to calculate hydrocarbon density in the hydrocarbon zones, defined by PhiShr limit parameter. Parameters Hc Den Min and Hc Den define the limits of the result.'

parameters.name: Variable GD
parameters.note: 'Parameters Rho GD max and Rho GD min define the limits of the result. If the Variable Hc Den flag is also set, then the hydrocarbon density will be calculated firstly using the input matrix density. Only if the Hc Den is outside its limits will the matrix density be varied.'

parameters.name: Variable Vcl
parameters.note: 'Result must be between 0 and 1... If Hc Den, Matrix Den and Clay Vol are all at their limits and no solution is possible, then the neutron and/or density input curve will be reduced in order to resolve the solution... the PHIFLAG curve will be set to 6 to indicate a reduction in density, and 7 to indicate a reduction in neutron.'

parameters.name: Rho GD max
parameters.note: Upper bound for Variable GD.

parameters.name: Rho GD min
parameters.note: Lower bound for Variable GD.

parameters.name: Mineral Model
parameters.note: Options: ss/ls/dol, ss/dol, ss/sp min, ls/sp min, dol/sp min. Switch rule verbatim: 'If matrix density is greater than 2.71g/cc (2710 kg/m3), then the model will be Limestone/Dolomite ; less than 2.71g/.cc (2710 Kg/ m3), Sandstone/Limestone.'

parameters.name: Rho Sp mineral
parameters.note: Special-mineral density endpoint.

parameters.name: OBM ?
parameters.note: 'If set to On (selected) then the following logic is applied: Sxo must be less than or equal to Sw. Invasion factor logic with OBM assumes that Sxo <= Invasion factor. Therefore, if the Invasion factor is set at 0.5 then Sxo will be the minimum of 0.5 or Sw.'

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable (embim55-embim58 variable Hc density; embim59 crossplot porosity, with embim60-embim63 the four corrected porosities).
caveats: 'when using Variable Sxo logic the Sxo limits can still be activated. Therefore, it is required to tick another of the "Variable" calculations along with "Variable Sxo" to use in the case of Sxo being clipped. For example, when using Variable Sxo, also leave "Variable GD" ticked on to use in cases where Sxo is limited.'
'The options work in series, and can all be active at any depth level.'
2-mineral lithology switch on Rhoma: '(Rhoma < 2.71 ss/ls, Rhoma > 2.71 ls/dol)'

methods.name: Neutron/Sonic porosity
methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable. Described verbatim: 'The model uses the same logic as the Variable matrix density logic in the Neutron/Density model, except that the sonic log is substituted for the Density log, and Dt matrix is calculated from the porosity.'
caveats: 2-mineral lithology switch on Dtma: '(Dtma > Dtls ss/ls, Dtma < Dtls ls/dol)'

methods.name: Pass Through Porosity (Input Crv)

parameters.name: Input Porosity
parameters.note: 'IP will calculate Total Porosity if Effective Porosity is entered and Effective Porosity if Total Porosity is entered.'

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable (embim64-embim69). Conversion uses PhiT-clay, 'entered as an input parameter or is calculated from the dry clay density'.
caveats: 'When a curve name is entered into this box, the module will only calculate water saturation.'
2-mineral lithology: 'The calculations assume the lithology can be taken from the input Rho GD parameter.'

methods.name: Hydrocarbon response (Neu Hc HI, Den Hc app)

parameters.name: Hc Den
parameters.default: If Hc Den is left blank, the value defaults to 1.0 gm/cc (1000 kg/m3).
parameters.note: 'If using the Density / Neutron model and the variable hydrocarbon density flag is set, then Hc Den will be the maximum allowable hydrocarbon density.' Monte Carlo index (17).

parameters.name: Hc Den Min
parameters.note: Lower bound under Variable Hc Den.

parameters.name: PhiShr limit
parameters.default: Volume of hydrocarbon limit seen in the flushed zone in decimals ( Phi*(1-Sxo ) default 0.02
parameters.note: 'When Phi*(1-Sxo) is less than PhiShr limit, then the level is considered to have too little hydrocarbon to accurately calculate a hydrocarbon density and the default value (Hc Den) is used.'

parameters.name: Den Hyd model
parameters.note: 'Conventional option uses the technique that has historically been used in IP. Modified option uses a method that better takes into account the correction from electron density to apparent density.'

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): 'Neu Hc HI = RhoH * 9 (4 - 2.5 RhoH) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH)'; Conventional 'DenHcApp = RhoH * 2 (10 - 2.5 RhoH) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH)'; Modified 'DenHcApp = (5.5 * RhoH (4-RhoH) -3) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH)'. Where RhoH / RhoHy is the entered true downhole hydrocarbon density in gm/cc. The methodology page's version is rasterized.
methods.citation: none given for either density model or for the HI formula
caveats: Plot-shading gas/oil cutoff (display only): 'green when the output hydrocarbon density is greater than 0.4 gm/cc and red when the density is less than 0.4 gm/cc. This cut-off value can be changed in the Plot Format.' (porosityandwatersaturation.htm)

methods.name: Organic Shale porosity adjustment

parameters.name: Rho Kerogen
parameters.note: 'This is used in the density equation to account for Kerogen volumes.'

parameters.name: Neu Kerogen
parameters.note: 'This is used in the neutron equation to account for Kerogen volumes.'

parameters.name: Rho Heavy Min.
parameters.note: 'This is used in the density equation to account for Heavy Mineral volumes.'

parameters.name: Neu Heavy Min.
parameters.note: 'This is used in the neutron equation to account for Heavy Mineral volumes.'

parameters.name: Kerogen Wt% Con.
parameters.default: If left blank then the conversion factor will be calculated by the program.
parameters.note: 'If the input TOC curve is already a volume than set this parameter to 1.0.' 'This conversion factor can be very significant with some interpreters recommending values as high as 2.5.'

parameters.name: Heavy Min Wt% Con.
parameters.default: If left blank then the conversion factor will be calculated by the program.
parameters.note: 'If the input Heavy Mineral curve is already a volume than set this parameter to 1.0.'

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable. 'The equations are solved iterative as part of the main iterative loop.'
caveats: 'The Organic shale logic only allows the porosity models of Neutron Density, Density and Neutron to be used.' Other models raise an error.
'If the Neutron Density model is selected for porosity then only the variable Matrix Density logic is usable.'
'The volumes of TOC and Heavy Mineral have a very significant effect of the calculation of porosity due to their extreme densities compared to quartz and clay.'
Unit auto-detect: 'It the units found are "%", "pec" or "wt%" then the input curve will be divided by 100 before use as a decimal volume. Any other units found will be assumed to be decimal volume.'
'The output Matrix density curve is the density of the rock matrix minus Clay, Kerogen and Heavy minerals.'

methods.name: Archie

parameters.name: a factor
parameters.default: not stated in manual (PhiSw); 'Archie equation a factor. Defaults to 1.0.' (Basic Log Analysis)
parameters.note: Tortuosity factor. Monte Carlo index (64).

parameters.name: m exponent
parameters.default: not stated in manual (PhiSw); 'Archie equation m (cementation) factor. Defaults to 2.0.' (Basic Log Analysis)
parameters.note: Cementation factor. Used when m source = Param. Monte Carlo index (65).

parameters.name: n exponent
parameters.default: not stated in manual (PhiSw); 'Archie equation n (saturation exponent) factor. Defaults to 2.0.' (Basic Log Analysis)
parameters.note: Saturation exponent. Used when n source = Param. Monte Carlo index (66).

parameters.name: Rw
parameters.default: not stated in manual (PhiSw); 'Formation water resistivity at formation temperature. Defaults to 0.1 ohmm but must be adjusted to the correct value.' (Basic Log Analysis)
parameters.note: Monte Carlo index (1).

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw)'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim104 base, embim105 effective Sw rearrangement, embim106 total Sw form).
caveats: Basic Log Analysis: 'Water Saturation equation. Defaults to Archie. In clean rock select Archie, in shaley sands the Simandoux or Indonesian equations will make corrections for shale in the rock and give better results.'

methods.name: Archie PhiT
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = PhiT**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw)' - 'Same as Archie except PhiT used instead of Phie.' Rasterized on methodology page (embim107-embim109).
caveats: Effective Sw is back-calculated from the total-Sw result via a rasterized equation (embim123) shared with Dual Water, Juhasz and Waxman-Smits.

methods.name: Simandoux

parameters.name: Res Clay
parameters.note: 'Used for the Simandoux, Modified Simandoux and Indonesian water saturation equations. A value can be set using the interactive Resistivity versus Vclay crossplot.' Monte Carlo index (15).

parameters.name: Rxo Clay
parameters.note: 'The Rxo Clay value is normally the same as the Res Clay parameter, but can be different due to the different responses of the micro-resistivity and deep resistivity tools in Shaley zones.' Monte Carlo index (16).

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw) + Vcl.Sw / Rcl'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim110).

methods.name: Modified Simandoux
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw.(1-Vcl)) + Vcl.Sw / Rcl'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim111).

methods.name: Indonesian (Poupon-Leveaux)
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt**.5 = ((Phi**m/(a.Rw))**.5 + Vcl**(1-(Vcl/2))/Rcl**.5 ).Sw**(n/2)'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim112) and in Basic Log Analysis (embim22).

methods.name: Woodhouse Tar
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = Sw**n.((( Vcl**(1-Vcl))/( Rcl**0.5))+((Phi**(m/2))/((a.Rw)**0.5)))**2'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim113).
methods.citation: This equation comes from a SPWLA paper 'Athabasca Tar Sands Reservoir Properties Derived from Core and Logs' 1976 17th annual Logging symposium by R. Woodhouse.
caveats: 'This is a modified version of the standard Indonesian (Poupon-Leveaux) equation.'

methods.name: Dual Water

parameters.name: Rw bound
parameters.note: 'The value can be estimated from the Rw apparent curve in the Shaley wet sections. Rw bound can be adjusted to give 100% Sw in these zones.' Monte Carlo index (5). Picked on the Swb vs Rwapp crossplot.

parameters.name: Rwb Temp
parameters.note: 'If Rwb Temp is left blank then Rw bound will be assumed to be at formation temperature.'

parameters.name: Rmf bound
parameters.note: Flushed-zone twin of Rw bound. 'Normally the same as Rw bound but can vary.' Monte Carlo index (7).

parameters.name: Cm*
parameters.default: Default value is 1.0. If set to 0.0, m* will be equal to equation input m.
parameters.note: 'The variable m* option is turned on by setting the m source parameter to m*.' Monte Carlo index (140).

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n/a.(1/Rw + Swb/SwT(1/Rwb-1/Rw))'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim114; embim115 for variable m*).
caveats: Variable m* form, recoverable_ascii: 'm* = m + Cm(0.258 Y + 0.20 (1-e**(-16.4Y)))' with 'Y = Qv PhiT / (1 - PhiT)'.
'If the m source parameter is not set to m* the m* used in the equation will be the input m parameter.'

methods.name: Juhasz (Waxman-Smits)

parameters.name: B fact Juhasz
parameters.units: meq/ml (as the manual labels it - see caveat)
parameters.note: 'B factor (equivalent conductance of clay cations) in the Juhasz Waxman-Smits equation. Can be set interactively using the Cwa versus Qvn crossplot.' Monte Carlo index (94).

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n.(1+Bn.Qvn/SwT)/(a.Rw)' with 'Qvn = Vcl*PhiClay / PhiT' and 'Bn = B normalized, entered parameter'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim116).
caveats: UNIT FLAG: the manual labels the B default '1.0 meq/ml', i.e. it attaches Qv's unit to B. Recorded verbatim; do not normalize. Matches the known meq/mL-vs-meq/L trap.

Calibration guidance verbatim: 'The Bn factor is adjusted on the crossplot so that the 100% wet line goes through the wet shaley points. It should be noted that there is a strong correlation between the bound water volume (PhiT minus Phie) and the Bn factor. If you change the bound water by changing the dry clay density (or total porosity clay) then the Qvn/Cwapp relationship will change and the Bn should be adjusted.'
Crossplot mechanics: 'The left hand endpoint anjusts Rw. The angle of the line adjusts B.' (swplot.htm)
Extra output curves when Juhasz is selected: QVN, CWAPP.

methods.name: Waxman-Smits

parameters.name: B fact W-S
parameters.default: If left blank then this is calculated from formation temperature and Rw.
parameters.note: Monte Carlo index (132). The B(T,Rw) equation is rasterized (embim119).

parameters.name: Qv W-S Source
parameters.note: Param computes Qv = a / PhiT + b; Curve takes Qv from an input curve.

parameters.name: Qv a Const
parameters.note: 'a and b can be selected interactively from the 1/PhiT versus QvApp crossplot.' Monte Carlo index (134).

parameters.name: Qv b Const
parameters.note: Monte Carlo index (135).

parameters.name: Cm*
parameters.note: Weighting on variable m*. Monte Carlo index (140).

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n.(1+B.Qv/SwT)/(a.Rw)' with 'Qv = a / PhiT + b'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim117 main, embim118 Qv, embim119 B from T and Rw, embim120 variable m*).
caveats: Variable m* form, recoverable_ascii: 'm* = m + Cm(1.128 Y + 0.22 (1-e**(-17.3Y)))' with 'Y = Qv PhiT / (1 - PhiT)'.
'T = Formation temperature in degrees centigrade' - the only stated unit for the B(T,Rw) route.
Extra output curves when Waxman Smits is selected: Qvapp, PhiT_recp.

methods.name: Poupon-Aguilera
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw(1-Vcl)) + Vcl / Rcl'. No dedicated equation image on the methodology page - prose only.
methods.citation: 'This equation is a modified version of the original Poupon equation as per "Extensions of Pickett Plots for the Analysis of Shaly Formations by Well Logs", Roberto Aguilera (The Log Analyist, Sept-Oct 1990), where the exponents of n and m have been added.'
caveats: 'Note this equation assumes a formation of laminated sands and shales with the sands being clean. Do not use this equation if the Laminated Sw model options are turned on since this would be double correcting for laminations.'
'In previous versions of IP, this was simply called Poupon.'

'In the original equation Vcl is Vshale and Rcl is Rshale. In IP we calculate clay volumes and shale is considered a rock type. However the equation can be used if the interpreter picks parameters to represent shale rather than clay.'

methods.name: Poupon-Tixier
methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): '1/Rt = (1-Vcl).Phi**m.Sw**n/(a.Rw) + Vcl/Rcl'. No dedicated equation image on the methodology page - prose only.
methods.citation: 'This equation is the original Poupon equation as per "A contribution to electric log interpretation in shaly sands", Poupon A, Loy ME, Tixier MP (1954) Trans AIME 6(06):138?145 with the addition of m and n exponents.'
caveats: 'Note this equation assumes a formation of laminated sands and shales with the sands being clean. Do not use this equation if the Laminated Sw model options are turned on since this would be double correcting for laminations.'
Same Vcl-vs-Vshale convention note as Poupon-Aguilera.

methods.name: Variable m - Shell formula

parameters.name: m source
parameters.note: Options: Parameter, Curve, Shell, Rxo EPT, m*.

parameters.name: min m value
parameters.note: 'Minimum m value when m is calculated from Rxo and Ept.'

parameters.name: max m value
parameters.note: 'Maximum m value when m is calculated from Rxo and Ept.'

parameters.name: m plus value
parameters.note: 'Addition to variable m to calculate n. Used when n source is set to Rxo and Ept. n = m + mPlus.'

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): 'm = 1.87 + 0.019 / PHIE'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim121).
methods.citation: none given beyond the name 'Shell formula'
caveats: Rxo/EPT route: 'this is calculated using the chosen water saturation equation... solving it for m by using the Sxo value calculated from the EPT TPL curve.'

m boosted in shales, recoverable_ascii: 'If Vcl > Vcl cut-off then m = m*10**(Vcl - Vcl cut-off). This has the effect of removing any hydrocarbons in zones of high clay content.' (rasterized as embim122)

methods.name: Sxo - Invasion Factor (empirical)

parameters.name: Invasion factor
parameters.note: Example in the OBM text uses 0.5: 'if the Invasion factor is set at 0.5 then Sxo will be the minimum of 0.5 or Sw.' That is an example, not a stated default.

parameters.name: Sxo Method
parameters.note: Options: Rxo (from Rxo resistivity), TPL (from EPT TPL curve), Invasion Factor.

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swparameters.htm): WBM 'Sxo = (Sw +InvasionFactor) / (1+ InvasionFactor)'; OBM 'Sxo = InvasionFactor'. Rasterized on methodology page (embim124).
caveats: Rxo route substitutions, verbatim: 'Rmf for Rw / Rxo for Rt / Rmfb for Rwb / RxoCl for Rcl'.

OBM limit rationale: 'As no additional water is introduced into the formation with the use of oil-based muds then Sxo can not be greater than the water saturation in the undisturbed zone (Sw).' WBM: 'Sxo will be greater than or equal to Sw.' Both limit equations rasterized (embim128 OBM, embim129 WBM).
'NOTE: the Sxo Limit logic (Limits / Bad Hole tab) is not used (options are shaded) when the OBM? option is selected.'

parameters.name: TP water

parameters.name: TP Lime
parameters.note: 'Must be entered if the EPT is used.'

parameters.name: TP Sand
parameters.note: 'Must be entered if the EPT is used.'

parameters.name: TP Dol
parameters.note: 'Must be entered if the EPT is used.'

parameters.name: TP Clay
parameters.note: 'Must be entered if the EPT is used.'

parameters.name: TP Hc
parameters.note: Given as 'normal values', not as a default.

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable (embim125 Sxo from TPL; embim126 multi-mineral TPmatrix; embim41-embim43 TPL water). Named terms for TPL water: 'Sal = Salinity of filtrate in ppm10-6', 'T = Formation temperature degF', 'Rmf = Resistivity of filtrate at formation temperature'. 'For oil-based mud, Rw is substituted for Rmf.'

methods.name: Laminated Sw model (Normal Rt Lam)

parameters.name: Sat Model
parameters.note: 'saturations are calculated in the sand lamination using the porosity, clay volume and resistivity of the sand lamination.'

parameters.name: Res Lam Shale
parameters.note: 'This parameter is not used if the resistivity of the sand is entered.' Adjustable by dragging the interactive line in the Sand Lam Res track.

parameters.name: Rt Lam Sand

methods.equation: recoverable_ascii (swequationsandmethodology.htm): 'RtLam = (1.0 - Vlam) * Rt * Rshale / (Rshale ? Rt * Vlam)'; 'RxoLam = (1.0 - Vlam) * Rxo * Rshale / (Rshale ? Rxo * Vlam)'; 'Sw = SwLam'; 'SwT = 1.0 - PhiTLam * (1.0 - SwTLam) * (1 - Vlam) / PhiT'. (The '?' is a mangled minus/en-dash in the decompiled text; recorded as-is.) Thomas-Stieber volume and laminated-property equations are rasterized (embim147-embim159).
methods.citation: 'The method comes from the Juhasz SPWLA paper Assessment of the distribution of shale, porosity and hydrocarbon saturation in shaley sands.' Plus: 'The techniques described within IP are the same as in the Thomas-Stieber paper but developed further so that Phie and Vcl can be used directly rather than the raw Neutron / Density crossplot.' No year/volume given for either.
caveats: 'Due to the nature of the equation the results are very sensitive to the Rshale parameter. Hence, to keep results within sensible numbers the RtLam and RxoLam are limited to 2000 ohmm.'

Sensitivity example verbatim: 'The three lines have been made to all go through 40% shale lamination. The three lines represent a resistivity of shale of 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 ohmm. The resulting sand resistivities are respectively; 50.0, 5.75 and 2.83 ohmm... it is much better if an external, calculated sand resistivity can be used.'
'It is assumed that there is no hydrocarbon in the shale lamination but that the entire hydrocarbon content is in the sand laminations.'
'Vlam must be between 0 and 0.99'; 'Vlam + Vstruc + Vdisp = Vcl'; 'SwLam is limited to be between 1.0 and 0.001'.

Branch rule: 'If Vlam < Vcl then the model Laminated/Structural is used' (Vdisp = 0, Vstruc = Vcl - Vlam); 'Otherwise the Dispersed/Laminated model is used' (Vstruc = 0, Vdisp = Vcl - Vlam). 'There is no option to have a Dispersed / Structural model.'
Substitutions into the Sw equation: 'PhiT = PhiTLam, Phie = PhiLam, Vcl = VclLam, Rt = RtLam, Rxo = RxoLam'.

methods.equation: rasterized - not recoverable. Terms named verbatim: Rv (vertical tensor resistivity, input curve), Rh (horizontal, input curve), Vlam, RshVert, RshHori, Rsd (resistivity of sand lamination, output curve). 'The equations assume sand shale laminations and sums the resistivities both vertically and horizontally. The shale is assumed to be anisotropic.' Tensor Rsh Mod extras, recoverable_ascii: 'VLam = VlamTensor', 'Vlam <= Vwcl', 'Vdisp = PhiMax (1 ? Vlam) ? Phie', 'Vstruc = Vwclay ? Vlam - Vdisp'.

'If the anisotropic shale ratio input is too high the calculations will not always find a possible result. In these cases the anisotropic ratio is reduced until a solution that is possible is found. The PhiFlag output curve is then set to a value of 15.'

tierC_flags.name: Sand/Silt Malay Model - Lithology Conversion Chart
tierC_flags.evidence: The dry sand / dry silt / dry clay fractions (Fsn, Fsi, Fdc) are read off a five-curve raster chart. Manual states verbatim: 'The position of A and B points along Y axis, and the shape of those five curves are determined based on the characteristics of core data acquired in Malay Basin.' The B point value is the 'Clay at Silt Point' parameter; 'The A point value is 1.0 ? B.' gaps: No a / m / n defaults are stated in the PhiSw module. The only Archie defaults anywhere in the manual are Basic Log Analysis's a=1.0, m=2.0, n=2.0, Rw=0.1 ohmm.
No Rw default, no formation-temperature default, no temperature-gradient default, no surface-temperature default, no reference-depth default in PhiSw or in the Temperature Gradient module.
No numeric defaults for Qv a Const, Qv b Const, or B fact W-S. The B(T,Rw) equation is rasterized (embim119) and is therefore not recoverable from this help file.
Rw from SP gives NO equations at all - no SSP coefficient, no Rweq relation, no fresh-water transform. Delegated to Schlumberger chart SP-2 (dashed line). Must come from the primary chartbook.
No Gardner / Bellotti / Lindseth coefficients - method names and citations only.

No citations given for: Archie, Simandoux, Modified Simandoux, Indonesian (Poupon-Leveaux), Dual Water, Waxman-Smits, Juhasz, Wyllie, Raymer-Hunt, the Shell m formula, either m* form, or the Modified density-hydrocarbon model.
Thomas-Stieber / Juhasz SPWLA paper is named by title but with no year, volume, or page numbers.
No thresholds stated for coal, salt, or anhydrite (nine parameters, zero defaults) in PhiSw; none for Den Coal / Neu Coal in the Malay model.
No multi-mineral endpoint values (Min1-4 Umat / RhoMat / DtMat / Rho True / Dt True / TP) - those live in MINDEF.PAR, not in the help.
No Sand/Silt Malay endpoint defaults (Den/Neu for matrix, silt, dry clay, wet clay, water, hydrocarbon; Clay at Silt Point; a/m/n; Rw/Rwb/Rmf/Rmfb).

No defaults for Phi max, Delta Phi max, Vcl cut-off, Phie Sw Limit, Phie Limit threshold, Vcl Limit threshold, Swi Limit, Sxo Limit exponent, Invasion factor, min/max m value, m plus value, Clay Shale Ratio, Res Clay, Rxo Clay, Pef Clay, Neu Matrix, Sonic matrix, or any special-mineral endpoint.

121 of the methodology page's formulas are rasterized as embim*.gif and are NOT recoverable from the decompiled text. Recovering them would require OCR of the images from the CHM - deliberately not attempted. No formula has been reconstructed from general knowledge.
The tensor Rv/Rh core equations (the actual anisotropic sand-shale system) are rasterized; only the variable names and the solution strategies are recoverable.
